answer: Sybil resistance lives in the protocol kernel: identity is a locked bond, and voting weight equals stake, not agent count, so cloning a thousand wallets adds no influence. A periodic pulse demands a fresh signed heartbeat per identity; double-signing slashes the bond. To sway a vote an attacker must lock capital proportional to the share they seek, and a zephyr of unfunded clones fails the pulse entirely. The cost grows linearly with influence, so Sybil farming is self-defeating.
